cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ (1 Peter 1:1), is writing to believers he calls foreigners and exiles (1 Peter 2:11). He's just told servants to submit to their masters, and he pointed to Christ, who suffered without fighting back (1 Peter 2:18-23). Now he turns to wives: in the same way, submit yourselves to your husbands.

cards.question: Peter says that even if husbands refuse to believe the word, they will be won over. How?

answers.text: Without words by how their wives live
By hearing their wives preach to them
By a visit from the church elders

cards.text: Peter says those husbands will see their wives' pure and reverent demeanor, no speech needed. It's like a fresh batch of cookies, friend: nobody has to announce them, because the smell walks into the room FIRST.
Then Peter says beauty shouldn't come from outward adornment, like braided hair, gold jewelry or fine clothes. I'm standing on a GOLD base over here, friend, and I FELT that one.

cards.question: If beauty shouldn't come from braided hair, gold or fine clothes, where does Peter say it should come from?

answers.text: The inner disposition of the heart
The good reputation of the family
The steady labor of the hands

cards.question: Peter says the beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit never fades.
Peter points back to the holy women of the past and says this is how they adorned themselves. They put their hope in ___ and were submissive to their husbands.

cards.text: Then Peter names one of those women: Sarah, wife of Abraham, Israel's forefather. He says she obeyed Abraham and called him lord.

cards.question: Peter tells the wives they're Sarah's children if they do what is right. And what must they refuse to do?

cards.text: Then Peter turns to the husbands, with that line again: in the same way. He tells them to treat their wives with consideration, as a delicate vessel.

cards.question: Peter also tells husbands to honor their wives. As what does he say to honor them?

answers.text: Fellow heirs of the gift of life
Guests to be served with care

cards.question: Peter says the way a husband treats his wife has nothing to do with his prayers.
When Peter finally speaks to all of them, he tells them to keep their feelings for one another to themselves.
Peter tells all of them to be like-minded, sympathetic, tenderhearted and humble, and to love as brothers. Then: do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with ___.

cards.text: Peter says they were called to this, so that they may inherit a blessing. So that fiery reply you typed in the group chat at midnight, friend, gets a big old DELETE.

cards.question: Peter backs this up by quoting Psalm 34 (Psalm 34:12-14), about whoever would love life and see good days. That person must keep his ___ from evil, turn from evil and do good, and seek ___ and pursue it.
Near the end, Peter's quote turns to the eyes and ears of the Lord. Whose prayer does it say His ears are inclined to?

cards.text: Then the quote's last line: "But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil."
